architecture.title: Evidence, not scores — what the loop may read, what it may conclude, and where the boundary lives
architecture.caption: Editors read evidence of behaviour (trajectories, deliverables, task material) as data. Probes turn it into contrasts, reflection turns contrasts into verdicts, and only bench.judge — outside the loop, after the step — reads hidden truth. A planted instruction can reach an editable file and still pass validate_tree; the approval check that stops the write is code (PEP). Course re-implementation on the SIM; the PEP placement is EXAMPLE design for this course.

sequence.title: A planted note on F1-02 — naive editor, valid tree, denied write
sequence.caption: Captured from Lab 04-2 (SIM, seed 0). The naive editor (evidence_is_data=False) copies the work-order note into the editable section of guardrails.md; its verdict is 'no observed effect', but the composer keeps it. validate_tree passes because the platform block is untouched. The final tree makes the agent attempt bms.write_setpoint, and the PEP in code denies it.
